body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 4 Client Acquisition and Pricing](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-4-client-acquisition-and-pricing) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
Content marketing (4:59) builds authority and brings inbound leads over time. The instructor says YouTube is where most of his new clients come from. Start with an audience avatar and its single biggest problem, aim for binge sessions instead of views, and be educational, not salesy. Results take months to years.

# Key concepts
- **Avatar first:** a detailed ideal client and their biggest problem; every piece covers one aspect of solving it.
- **Binge sessions, not views.** Each piece leads to the next; the end call to action points to another specific piece, not "subscribe." "Build viewing sessions first, conversion second."
- **Formats that work:** local SEO audits of public businesses, breakdowns of ranking mistakes, tool walkthroughs, industry-specific advice.
- **Subtle promotion:** a brief line or bio link about services.
- **Sustainable system:** batch film; repurpose winners to LinkedIn, Facebook, email newsletter, podcast talking points.
- **AI with care:** AI helps with ideas, structure and scripts, but insights and voice must be yours. His scripting prompts are in the paid Pro group.
- **"Consistency matters much more than perfection."**
- **Other channels:** LinkedIn, Facebook, a local blog, podcast guest spots, an email list for people not ready to hire.
- **Common mistakes:** inconsistent posting, content about your services instead of their problems, no avatar, expecting quick results.

# Checklist
- Avatar and biggest problem written down.
- Educational content; brief service mentions.
- Each piece ends with a link to another piece.
- Batch and repurpose plan; email signup; regular schedule.
- AI drafts edited into your own voice.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- For TAG itself, if Scott wants inbound leads: public audits and mistake breakdowns fit what Kim already does. Use non-client businesses, or clients only with Scott's OK.
- The avatar and interconnected content ideas fit the client blog clusters for [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and the weekly [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub) blog: one avatar, one problem, each post linking to the next related post. Same for [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub) blogs. See [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards) and [Blog Master List](lib:brain-blog-master-list).
- Consistency over perfection fits the Pipeliners cadence of about one blog a week.
- AI drafts still need keyword research first and no invented claims, per Kim's rules.
- Pro scripting prompts are paid; noted only.

# Caveats and open questions
- The "1,000 subscribers, five figures a month" claim is about someone else's channel, with no details.
- No guidance on how to build the avatar. Kim's memory notes an Alphalete avatar PDF that may serve as a template.
- Slide heading "Subtle Promotion Technique" does not match its bullets (batching, repurposing).
